messages.body_plain:
Hello,  Mike.

Thanks for your kind advice and apologies for my *very* late reply. It so happened that when your message arrived, it was automatically moved from the email inbox to my R-pkg-develop mailbox, but somehow I did not spot it until now. I have no explantion for this, ...except that this looks like a case of ageing effect!

I have now made the changes that you suggested. Specifically, in the DESCRIPTION file, there are these lines

Depends: R (>= 4.2.0),
Imports: sn (>= 2.1.3), ggplot2 (>= 3.4.2), methods, mnormt (>= 2.1.2),  patchwork (>= 1.1.2) 

and in NAMESPACE there is

import(sn)
import(ggplot2)

Unfortunately, when I run  R CMD check --as-cran  gg.sn_0.1.1.tar.gz, I now get an error message whenever an example of the documentation uses a function of package sn, such as 

> f1 <- makeSECdistr(dp=c(3,2,5), family="SN", name="First-SN")
Error in makeSECdistr(dp = c(3, 2, 5), family = "SN", name = "First-SN") :    could not find function ?makeSECdistr"

Even if I include a line like

importFrom(sn, dp2cp, makeSECdistr, modeSECdistr, marginalSECdistr)  

in NAMESPACE, still the error persists.

The only solution which worked was to write 
f1 <- sn::makeSECdistr(dp=c(3,2,5), family="SN", name="First-SN?)
but this make the usage and coding less smooth.

Am I missing something? 

Best regards,

Adelchi

messages.body_plain:
A while ago there was discussion on this list about new behavior in
R-4.6 of update.packages to reinstall packages if the "Built"
timestamp has changed. This leads to many unnecessary updates for e.g.
Windows users because CRAN rebuilds most Windows binary packages every
few days.

Maybe it makes sense to let users opt-in to this behavior via the
existing 'checkBuilt' parameter. This would be a trivial change:
https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/338/changes

messages.body_plain:
The discussion continued on the issue[1]. Quick summary: checkBuilt is a misnomer since it is documented to only check the major R version and was used to upgrade between R versions - it is too late to change that now. The current behavior was introduced specifically to avoid broken libraries when dependencies are not updated when they need to be and thus it has to be the default. A package binary should only change if there was an update. We now have a mechanism to flag rev dep changes to prevent unnecessary re-builds, but it is not been used everywhere yet so the over-eager re-building is a conservative approach to used before that mechanism was in place, but go away eventually.

Cheers,

The examples in a help page are evaluated in the user's environment. 
They don't have access to all the symbols that functions in your package 
can see, only the ones that the user can see.

If you import sn, then its functions are available within your package, 
but they aren't available to users.

So the best solution to your problem is the one you found (i.e. use 
sn::makeSECdistr).  It would also work to use "library(sn)" in the 
example, but that modifies the user's search list, so it's not such a 
good idea.  (I don't remember if CRAN will object to it, but it might.)
